problem: How supervised learning (BC) and reinforcement learning (PPO) differ in zero-shot generalization is poorly understood, and prior comparisons often run RL on top of an SL-pretrained model, which confounds the comparison.
motivation: Both SL and RL are used to train general-purpose agents and foundation models, yet it is unclear how much generalization each gives and by what mechanism. Habitat PointNav is a testbed with geometric and visual variation where both any-path success (SR) and shortest-path success (SPL) can be measured, so that different generalization strategies can be separated.
key_idea: TD-based RL generalizes by combinatorially stitching fragments of past (mostly failed) trajectories into new solutions, whereas BC generalizes by imitating the common patterns of successful (optimal) trajectories.
insight: Extra optimal demonstrations let BC match PPO in SPL, but a success-rate gap remains, and BC's SPL equals its SR while PPO's SPL is below its SR. This suggests BC only finds shortest-path-like solutions, while PPO finds many non-shortest feasible paths. Training on more scenes improves unseen-scene generalization but hurts unseen (s0,g) and memorization performance, especially for BC. These conclusions are supported by figures and a hypothesis rather than a direct test of the stitching mechanism.
method: Task: Habitat PointNav on Gibson with a relative goal (an instruction-following-like formulation), egocentric visual observations, and discrete actions (stop, forward 0.25 m, turn ±10°).

PPO: trained from scratch, DD-PPO-style shared recurrent actor-critic, with a dense reward (success 2.5 + geodesic distance change + time penalty -0.0001), learning from its own trajectories including failed ones.
BC: same recurrent actor architecture without the critic, trained by maximum likelihood on shortest-path-planner optimal trajectories (2000 (s0,g) pairs per scene).
Evaluation protocol: three settings (seen (s0,g), unseen (s0,g) in training scenes, unseen scenes), actions sampled from the policy rather than greedy, metrics SR and SPL.
Augmented BC: adds 2000 more non-overlapping optimal trajectories per scene to test whether more data closes the gap.
Scene-count ablation: train on 1 vs 4 scenes to study the trade-off between visual and geometric generalization.
Guidelines: max-entropy RL and multimodal policies for RL; training SL on varied-quality and suboptimal data.

setting.backbone: Recurrent (RNN) actor-critic policy for PPO (DD-PPO architecture); the same recurrent actor for BC, trained from scratch
setting.training_data: 4 Gibson training scenes, 2000 (s0,g) pairs per scene (8000 in total); PPO collects its own online rollouts; BC uses shortest-path optimal trajectories (plus 2000 more per scene for augmented BC)
setting.observation: egocentric visual observation + relative point goal
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: stop, move forward 0.25 m, turn left 10°, turn right 10°
setting.privileged: none at test time (the ground-truth map is used during training only, to compute the geodesic-distance reward and the optimal BC trajectories)

numbers.eval_set_note: unseen-scenes evaluation on the full Gibson validation set: 994 (s0,g) pairs from 14 scenes; agents trained on 4 training scenes
numbers.extra: trained on only 4 scenes; actions sampled, not greedy; success within 0.2 m; the unseen-(s0,g) SR of 96.75% is on training scenes, not this split
numbers.evidence: Results are only shown in figures; the text gives PPO 96.75% zero-shot success rate in the unseen (s0,g) task.

numbers_note: Results are given mainly in figures (bar charts). The text prints only a few numbers: BC ~96% SPL and SR on seen pairs, PPO 13% lower SPL on seen pairs, and PPO 96.75% SR on unseen (s0,g). The numbers entry has empty metrics because no exact table values are printed for unseen scenes.
results: PPO outperforms BC in both zero-shot settings (unseen (s0,g) and unseen scenes) on SR and SPL. BC is better at memorization (~96% vs PPO 13% lower SPL on seen pairs). PPO reaches 96.75% zero-shot SR on unseen (s0,g). Augmented BC nearly matches PPO's SPL but stays well below it in SR.
limitations: Small-scale study: 4 training scenes, one task (PointNav), and one RL and one SL algorithm, with results shown only in figures and no statistics.
The stitching mechanism is hypothesized rather than directly verified, and the proposed guidelines (max-entropy RL, multimodal SL) are untested.
The relative-goal task is close to instruction following and comes with dense shaped rewards from a ground-truth map, which may limit how far the findings transfer to other goal-conditioned settings.
